Russell Brand Makes Wild Katy Perry Confession In Newly Revealed Deposition Russell Brand 's deposition in a New York sexual assault lawsuit is drawing fresh attention after the actor said he could not rule out having exposed himself to people without their consent. The testimony also covered his former marriage to Katy Perry , his public reputation for promiscuity, and his behavior during the years surrounding the filming of "Arthur."
 The ongoing civil case was brought by a woman who worked as an extra on the movie. Brand denies her allegations, and his broader comments about past conduct do not amount to an admission of the specific assault she alleges.
 Russell Brand Says He Cannot Rule Out Past Exposure
 News Licensing / MEGA
 According to deposition transcripts obtained by the Daily Mail , Brand was questioned under oath in Manhattan in 2025. Portions of that testimony were subsequently made public through court filings. Asked whether he had ever exposed himself to anyone without consent, Brand said he could not give an absolute denial.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Well, the truth is, I feel like I must have done, even though I don't really remember it and I find the idea embarrassing in quite a number of ways," he replied. "But I, you know, I can't, I couldn't concretely and absolutely rule that out."
 The questioning referenced a radio segment in which his former co-host, Matt Morgan, had joked about Brand exposing himself to a woman at a recording studio. His answer concerned possible past conduct generally, rather than confirming the plaintiff's account of what happened during filming.
 The 'Arthur' Lawsuit Centers On Alleged On-Set Assault
 MEGA
 The plaintiff, identified as Jane Doe, alleges Brand exposed himself to her in front of cast and crew while filming at Manhattan's Le Cirque restaurant in July 2010. She further alleges that he later sexually assaulted her in a bathroom.
 Brand has maintained that his sexual encounters were consensual.
 Advertisement Advertisement A published New York Supreme Court decision confirms that the woman brought the action under the Adult Survivors Act and named Brand, Warner Bros. and other production companies as defendants. The decision concerns a dispute over expert testimony, rather than a ruling on whether the alleged assault occurred.
 The New York proceedings are separate from Brand's British criminal case, in which he received a sentence of 10 years and six months earlier this month for rape and sexual assault.
 Russell Brand received an unexpected lifeline as Google reportedly refused to delete his prison video. 
 Russell Brand's "not guilty" prison message backfired as the U.K. government targeted his YouTube channel. 
 The family of Russell Brand's wife is reportedly "determined to get her to see the truth" amid her "blind faith." 
 Russell Brand was reportedly furious after prison staff seized his hair-loss pills, allegedly leaving him at risk of balding within three to four weeks. 
 Katy Perry Marriage Comes Up During Questioning
 Xavier Collin/Image Press Agency/MEGA
 Lawyers also questioned Brand about his relationship with Perry, whom he married in October 2010. Their marriage ended in 2012. When asked whether he was married during the filming of "Arthur," Brand did not immediately provide a clear timeline.
 Advertisement Advertisement "Whilst I, of course, it wouldn't be difficult for me to find out whether or not I was married, because it would be on the internet somewhere, I'm assuming," he said. "I was, what I do know is that I was in a relationship with, as you know, obviously a very high-profile woman."
 Brand then described his feelings during the marriage. "And even when I was married to her, I was sort of drowning in love," he said.
 The alleged July 2010 incident occurred before their wedding. Perry is not accused of wrongdoing in the account.
 Brand Revisits His Notorious Public Reputation
 PRPP/PictureLux / MEGA
 The deposition also returned to the persona Brand cultivated during his rise to fame. When a lawyer mentioned that The Sun had named him "Shagger of the Year" three times, Brand acknowledged that he once valued the recognition. "Outside of this context, that was a very proud accolade of mine," he said.
 Advertisement Advertisement He also discussed what he described as a recurring pattern in his behavior when he was not in love. "If I wasn't in love with someone probably all the way up 'til this marriage with my wife Laura, there were, we have a trend of deterioration, periods of that kind of excitement for a long while, probably all the way up to, I reckon, 2015, maybe," he testified. "Sort of, like, a ten-year period, really. A ten-year period."
 Brand married his current wife, Laura Gallacher, in 2017.
 Production Questions Extend Beyond Brand Himself
 News Licensing / MEGA
 Lawyers also asked whether Brand had alerted anyone at the studio or production companies to allegations of sexual misconduct. He maintained there "was nothing of that nature" and "nothing to discuss."
 Separately, Brand confirmed that his Alcoholics Anonymous sponsor visited the "Arthur" set. He also said he attended meetings with someone connected to Warner Bros. or another production company, but declined to identify that person out of respect for their anonymity.
 Advertisement Advertisement The production's knowledge and handling of Brand's conduct remain relevant to the claims against the corporate defendants. Variety previously reported that Warner Bros. had offered to disclose hours of outtake footage in connection with the litigation.
 The civil case remains ongoing, with the deposition forming part of the evidence being examined rather than a final determination of the plaintiff's allegations.
